name: Landlord ombudsman complaint workflow
demand: The trigger is credible but the exact timing is still conditional: the government expects mandatory membership in 2028, after the scheme is ready and landlords receive notice; the 2026 regulations establish a framework, not a precise start date (https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/renters-rights-act-2025-implementation-roadmap/implementing-renters-rights-act-2025-our-roadmap-for-reforming-the-private-rented-sector, https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2026/1033/made, https://publications.parliament.uk/pa/ld5902/ldselect/ldsecleg/3/305.htm). Current market proxies: England had 5.03 million private-rented dwellings at 31 March 2025, while HMRC counted 2.88 million UK unincorporated landlords declaring rental income in 2024/25 (https://www.gov.uk/government/statistics/dwelling-stock-estimates-in-england-2025/dwelling-stock-estimates-england-31-march-2025, https://www.gov.uk/government/statistics/property-rental-income-statistics/property-rental-income-statistics-2026). Neither is an exact count of eligible English landlord buyers: the HMRC figure is UK-wide and excludes incorporated businesses and some landlords below tax-reporting thresholds. Complaint-specific search volume, active users, app installs, and future Ombudsman complaint volumes are unverified. As a broad category proxy only, Google Play lists Landlord Studio at 50K+ downloads and its vendor says 80,000+ landlords use it; these figures do not validate demand for complaint software (https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.mozzarellalabs.landlordstudio, https://www.landlordstudio.com/uk).
prices: A near-direct pre-launch offer, Dealtwith, advertises £6.99/month for up to two tenancies and £2.99/month per additional tenancy; its page says the iOS and Android apps are still preparing for release (https://dealtwith.co.uk/pricing). Landlord Studio advertises a free plan for up to three units and Pro at £12/month plus VAT (https://www.landlordstudio.com/uk/pricing). Landlord Vision lists a £19.97/month Starter plan for four tenancies; higher plans include a tenant service desk, correspondence tracking and work orders (https://www.landlordvision.co.uk/landlord-software-pricing.html). These are advertised prices, not proof of sales.

revenue_proof.claim: No verified revenue, paid-user count or transaction amount found for this proposed PRS complaint product. Weak adjacent-category signal only: a Trustpilot-verified Landlord Vision reviewer wrote that they had started a subscription; the review does not disclose a payment or amount.
revenue_proof.claim_event_date: 2026-09-16 (review date; purchase and payment dates unverified)

copy_speed: High. Dealtwith already advertises timestamped repair and issue records, evidence exports and landlord-tenant messaging at a low monthly price, though its apps are listed as coming soon and its launch date is unverified (https://dealtwith.co.uk/, https://dealtwith.co.uk/pricing). Adjacent entrants since April 2026 include Stead, in closed beta from May 2026 with a landlord compliance pack, and Landlord Vision's mobile app, which a review dated 5 August 2026 describes as launched in 2026; neither is a confirmed PRS-ombudsman-only product (https://stead.space/press, https://apps.apple.com/gb/app/landlord-vision/id6760894389). Exact launch dates for a dedicated PRS complaint-workflow competitor are unverified.
platform_risk: High. The government says the Ombudsman will offer landlords complaint-handling tools, guidance and training, and is considering information sharing with the PRS Database; parliamentary scrutiny says the government intends one scheme and prefers the Housing Ombudsman Service as administrator (https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/renters-rights-act-2025-implementation-roadmap/implementing-renters-rights-act-2025-our-roadmap-for-reforming-the-private-rented-sector, https://publications.parliament.uk/pa/ld5902/ldselect/ldsecleg/3/305.htm). The Housing Ombudsman's existing social-housing landlord portal already provides case records, tasks, deadlines and evidence uploads, but its applicability to private landlords is unverified (https://www.housing-ombudsman.org.uk/landlords-info/interactive-portal-for-landlords/portal-user-guide/). A free or bundled official tool could absorb much of the proposed workflow; API access and the final scheme administrator are unverified.
defensible_asset: Weak today. A maintained, versioned England-specific rules checklist and a landlord-authorised chronology of reports, responses, evidence and outcomes could create some switching friction. The legal rules and government guidance are public, and competing products already advertise similar records and exports, so neither is a strong exclusive moat (https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/renters-rights-act-2025-implementation-roadmap/implementing-renters-rights-act-2025-our-roadmap-for-reforming-the-private-rented-sector, https://dealtwith.co.uk/, https://www.landlordvision.co.uk/landlord-software-pricing.html). Proprietary data, distribution partnerships and durable switching costs are unverified.
build_effort: Moderate product build; effort estimate unverified. A narrow MVP needs secure landlord and tenant access, complaint intake, evidence uploads, a dated case timeline, reminders, response drafts and exportable case records. Agents could automate classification, document extraction, chronology summaries, reminders, subscription support and PDF assembly; landlords should approve substantive responses and decisions. Security, privacy, support and keeping English rules current are the main ongoing burdens.
channel: Use inbound SEO and search ads for complaint-log and evidence-preparation searches, with a free template or sample case report leading to self-serve signup; a founder face or personal brand is unnecessary. Do not cold-email, text or DM individual landlords or sole traders: ICO guidance treats sole traders as individual subscribers, and electronic mail includes social-media DMs; unsolicited electronic marketing to individuals generally requires consent or a valid soft opt-in (https://ico.org.uk/for-organisations/direct-marketing-and-privacy-and-electronic-communications/business-to-business-marketing/, https://ico.org.uk/for-organisations/direct-marketing-and-data-protection/marketing-and-data-protection-in-detail/).
owner_hours_per_week: The <=5-hour/week limit is unverified. It is a design target that depends on self-service onboarding, low support demand and no bespoke legal or case-handling service.
desk_test: Within one day, make a clearly labelled concept page with a clickable complaint timeline and sample evidence export, display the £6.99/month price anchor already advertised by Dealtwith, and invite opt-in interest through a landlord community that permits research posts. Ask interested landlords to commit to a paid pilot or state what they currently use; count qualified commitments rather than likes. Do not send cold DMs or emails. No conversion benchmark is verified.
red_flags: This survives the statutory-trigger check, but it is not yet a validated business. The most direct competitor already advertises nearly the same workflow, official tools may overlap, and complaint-specific demand and paid use remain unverified. A £6.99/month adjacent price suggests limited room for labour-intensive support. The 0 automation figure means no measured share is available, not that a product has been observed operating at zero automation; the >=50% automation and <=5-hour/week constraints remain unproven.
